name: Chicken Enchiladas
method: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add the chicken and diced bell pepper and cook for 10-12 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, in a bowl mix the chopped tomatoes, salsa, dried oregano, dried basil and ground cumin.
Stir half of the tomato mixture into the cooked chicken and pepper.
Warm the tortilla wraps in the microwave for 15 seconds.
Place the tortillas in a baking dish, spoon the chicken mixture and a little grated cheese into the centre of each, and roll up.
Pour the remaining tomato mixture over the rolled tortillas and scatter the remaining cheese on top.

standard: Bake at 180°C (fan) for 20 minutes, until the cheese has melted and the sauce is bubbling.
fromFrozen: Bake from frozen at 200°C (fan) for 50 minutes, until piping hot throughout, the cheese has melted and the sauce is bubbling.

name: Chicken nuggets

ingredients.prep: skinless and boneless, cut into cubes

method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / gas mark 6.
Combine the breadcrumbs, grated parmesan, dried thyme and black pepper on a large plate or in a food bag.
Toss the chicken cubes in the melted butter, then turn them in the crumb mixture until well coated.
Place on a baking sheet and bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes, until crisp and cooked through.
To freeze, leave to cool completely, then transfer to a labelled freezer bag or container.

standard: Or, if reheating from chilled, warm through in an oven at 180°C (160°C fan) / gas mark 4 for 8-10 minutes, until piping hot throughout.
fromFrozen: Reheat from frozen in an oven at 200°C (180°C fan) / gas mark 6 for 12-15 minutes, until crisp and piping hot throughout.

name: Chicken, mushroom and spinach lasagne
method: Add the chicken breasts to a large saucepan with the bay leaves, cover with cold water, bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer for 10-15 minutes, until cooked through.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and mushrooms and cook for 7-8 minutes, until the mushrooms have released their liquid.
Stir in the spinach and cook until wilted right down. Season with salt and pepper and remove from the heat.
Lift out the cooked chicken (discard the water and bay leaves), shred it with two forks, then stir it through the mushroom and spinach mixture and set aside.
Make the cheese sauce: melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, slowly, so that it never bubbles.
Add all of the flour and mix to a smooth paste, then leave it for a minute.
Pour in all of the milk and turn the heat up to medium-high.
Keep stirring until all of the paste has dissolved: scrape it off the spoon and take the spoon right around the bottom and sides of the pan.
Keep stirring until the sauce comes up to a bubble, then turn off the heat.
Add the grated cheddar and stir until it has melted and dissolved into the sauce.

Layer up in a large ovenproof dish: a layer of the chicken mixture, then lasagne sheets, then cheese sauce. Repeat until everything is used up, finishing with lasagne sheets topped with a final layer of cheese sauce.
Mix the grated parmesan, dried basil and breadcrumbs together and scatter over the top.
To freeze, cover the dish tightly with cling film and then foil.

standard: Bake at 180°C (fan 160°C) / gas mark 4 for 45-50 minutes, until piping hot throughout and golden on top. Cover with foil if it browns too quickly.
fromFrozen: Bake from frozen at 180°C (fan 160°C) / gas mark 4 for 1 hour to 1 hour 10 minutes, until piping hot throughout. Cover with foil if it browns too quickly.

name: Chocolate chip cookies
method: Preheat the oven to 160°C fan and line several large baking sheets with baking paper.
Place the butter and both sugars in a large bowl and whisk together until pale and creamy.
Whisk the eggs and vanilla extract into the mixture until smooth.
Sift in the flour and bicarbonate of soda and beat together until well mixed, then stir in the chocolate chips.
Drop 12 large spoonfuls of the mixture onto the prepared baking sheets, spacing them well apart.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, until set and golden brown.
Leave to cool on the baking sheets for 2-3 minutes, then transfer the cookies to a wire rack and leave to cool completely.
To freeze, make sure the cookies are completely cold, then wrap them individually in cling film.

standard: Serve warm or wait for them to cool.
fromFrozen: Defrost in the microwave for 1 minute, then heat on high for 15 seconds.

name: Potato dauphinoise

ingredients.prep: large, Maris Piper, peeled and sliced as thinly as possible

method: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) / gas mark 4 and grease a shallow baking dish with butter.
Peel the potatoes and slice as thinly as possible, ideally using a mandolin or the slicing blade of a food processor.
Put the cream, milk, garlic and dried rosemary in a large pan with a generous grinding of salt and pepper. Place over a low heat, stirring occasionally, until the mixture is warmed but not boiling.
Add the potato slices to the pan, ensuring they are all submerged in the liquid, and leave to cook for 8-10 minutes, until just tender but still holding their shape.
Remove from the heat, then gently tip the mixture into the prepared baking dish, spreading out the potatoes so that they cover the surface in an even layer.
Sprinkle the grated gruyere over, then bake in the oven for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are cooked and the sauce has thickened.

If you are making this to freeze, remove it from the oven before the top has browned, as it will be baked again later. If you are eating it now, leave it until the top is beautifully golden and bubbling.

To freeze, set aside until cooled, then freeze the dauphinoise whole or cut into individual portions. Cover with a layer of clingfilm followed by a layer of foil, label and freeze flat for up to 3 months.

standard: Serve hot as an accompaniment to roast meats and vegetables, or a big bowl on its own.
If reheating from chilled, bake at 180°C (160°C fan) / gas mark 4 for 15-20 minutes, until piping hot throughout.
fromFrozen: Defrost fully, then bake at 180°C (160°C fan) / gas mark 4 for 15-20 minutes, until piping hot throughout.
Or cook from frozen: bake at 180°C (160°C fan) / gas mark 4 for 30 minutes, ensuring the dauphinoise is piping hot before serving.

name: Roasted red pepper soup
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / gas 6.
Put the halved tomatoes, quartered onion and chopped peppers in a roasting tin, toss with the olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Nestle in the garlic cloves.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, until all the veg has softened and slightly caramelised.
Squeeze the garlic cloves out of their skins into the tin and discard the skins.
Mix the red wine vinegar into the tin, then blend everything with a stick or bullet blender, adding enough water to loosen to your preferred consistency (about 150ml).
Leave to cool, then divide between freezer containers and freeze.

standard: Reheat gently in a pan or the microwave, stirring occasionally, until piping hot throughout.
Taste for seasoning, then ladle into bowls to serve.
fromFrozen: Microwave on the defrost setting for about 6 minutes.
Then microwave on high in three 1-minute bursts, stirring between each, until piping hot throughout. Transfer to a jug as soon as the soup is loose enough to come away from the container.

name: Salmon fried rice
method: Cook the rice in a pan of boiling water over a medium heat according to packet instructions. Once cooked, drain, rinse and set aside.

Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat, then add the salmon and cook for 3 minutes, removing and discarding the skin as the salmon cooks. Don't worry if the salmon flesh starts to break up as it cooks, as this helps it distribute through the finished dish.

Add the carrot, onion and bell pepper, then stir to combine. Using a wooden spoon or spatula, push the salmon and vegetable mixture to the side of the pan, then pour the beaten eggs into the centre and scramble them as they cook.
Add the rice to the pan along with the soy sauce, then stir everything until the salmon, vegetables and eggs are well distributed throughout and the rice is piping hot. Remove from the heat.
To freeze: set the rice aside until cooled to room temperature, then spoon into a labelled freezer bag or freezer-proof dish and freeze flat.

standard: Serve straight away, spooned into bowls.
Or, if reheating from chilled, warm through in a pan or microwave for 3-4 minutes, until piping hot.
fromFrozen: Defrost fully in the fridge, then reheat in a microwave or pan for 3-4 minutes, until piping hot.
Or cook from frozen in an oven preheated to 180°C (fan 160°C) / gas mark 4 for 30 minutes, until piping hot.

name: Spinach pasta bake
method: Place the penne in a large pan and pour over boiling water to cover. Cook according to packet instructions until just tender.
While the pasta is cooking, heat the olive oil in another pan over medium heat, then add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring, for 1 minute, until softened.
Add the chopped tomatoes, dried basil and dried oregano and stir to combine. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer while you prepare the other elements.
When the pasta is almost cooked, add the spinach to the pan and cook for 1 minute, until wilted, then drain and rinse the pasta and spinach through a colander.

Transfer the pasta and spinach mixture to a large baking dish. Pour over the sauce, then add all of the ricotta and half of the mozzarella. Stir the mixture until really well combined, then scatter over the remaining mozzarella and all of the parmesan.

standard: Bake at 180°C (fan 160°C) / gas mark 4 for 25-30 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Serve hot.
fromFrozen: Defrost overnight in the fridge, then cook as above.
Or cook from frozen: double the cooking time, covering with foil if the top starts to catch, and ensure the dish is piping hot before serving.
